messages:
Sam: Quick follow-up from today's RFC — we need to firm up the adapter surface between hosted / dedicated / private. I put together a short checklist of things I think matter: auth model, telemetry contract, config translation, rollout semantics, and failure/fallback behavior. Can folks sanity-check?

Jules: +1. My big worry is implicit behavior in translation. e.g., hosted allows token-scope features we can't expose in on-prem. Need explicit opt-outs.

Maria: Agree. For auth we should standardize on two modes: bearer token (for hosted) and mTLS / signed tokens (for private). Adapter should expose an AuthCapability boolean so control plane can surface allowed flows.

Kai: Also think about credential rotation. Private deploys will often have offline KMS; adapters must support a "rotate-now" hook. Maybe API: POST /_adapter/rotate-keys -> returns 202 + job id.

Sam: Good call. I sketched a minimal capability schema we can use to declare what an adapter supports. Example below:

```json
{
  "capabilities": ["auth:bearer","auth:mtls","telemetry:span","telemetry:metrics","model-pinning","kv-cache"],
  "config_map": {
    "batching": "continuous|disabled",
    "quantization_profile": "q8_0|q4_0|fp16",
    "fallback": "region|model-variant|queue"
  },
  "hooks": ["rotate-keys","health-check","drain"]
}
```

Jules: Love it. Two notes: 1) telemetry:span implies we can attach trace IDs; private clusters may scrub metadata — add a "telemetry:scrub-level" field. 2) model-pinning needs a version semantics (exact vs semver-range).

Leo: On rollout semantics: we can't assume same canary windows across environments. Suggest adapters expose "rollout_controls": {"canary_supported": true, "max_canary_percent": 50}. Control plane enforces safe defaults but can read adapter hints.

Maria: For failure semantics, clarify the difference between transient errors and capacity-denied. I propose adapter error codes map to our control-plane categories: OK, TRANSIENT, CAPACITY, PERMISSION, CONFIG. Include examples in spec.

Kai: OpsBot created a ticket for the key rotation hook: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-4123 :ticket: (auto note)

OpsBot: Deploy reminder — integration tests for adapter surface will run on staging in 45m.

Sam: One implementation tradeoff: do we require adapters to accept our canonical config (we translate) or force them to implement a tiny translator library? I prefer translation on control-plane side to keep adapters thin, but that increases surface testing. Thoughts?

Jules: Control-plane translation is OK if we version the translation rules and provide a conformance test-suite. If adapters change, they re-run the suite.

Maria: +1. Conformance suite should include: auth flows, trace continuity, cold-start latency under batch, and kv-cache prefix correctness. Keep tests small and fast.

Leo: Long-term refactor idea: plugin manifest + wasm validators for translation rules. That lets private customers vet translations before applying. Might be heavier but safer for regulated customers.

Sam: Nice. Action items: 1) Maria/Jules draft capability schema with scrub-level & pin semantics (due EOD). 2) Kai add rotate-keys endpoint to INF-4123 and sketch job lifecycle. 3) Leo prototype rollout_controls shape and conformance tests list. I'll follow up with a pared-down RFC update. :thumbsup:
